user_input: How long is the initial period of stay granted for an O-1 visa?
reference: The initial period of stay for an O-1 nonimmigrant is up to three years. USCIS then grants extensions in increments of up to one year, based on the time needed to accomplish the initial event or activity.
reference_contexts: Initial Period of Stay: Up to three years. Extension of Stay: We will determine the time you need to accomplish the initial event or activity in increments, up to one year.

user_input: Which form does an F-1 student file to get a work permit for OPT?
reference: To work on OPT, an F-1 student must apply for an Employment Authorization Document by filing Form I-765, Application for Employment Authorization. Employment can begin only once the EAD is issued and valid.
reference_contexts: To request an EAD, you generally must file Form I-765, Application for Employment Authorization.
Submit the Form I-765, Application for Employment Authorization, up to 90 days before your current OPT employment authorization expires

user_input: At minimum, how long does the initial H-1B electronic registration period stay open each year?
reference: The initial H-1B registration period runs for a minimum of 14 calendar days each fiscal year, after which USCIS runs the selection process on properly submitted registrations. Exact dates are announced by USCIS each year, so confirm the current season's dates on the H-1B Cap Season page.
reference_contexts: The initial registration period is for a minimum of 14 calendar days each fiscal year. USCIS then runs the H-1B selection process to select unique beneficiaries based on properly submitted electronic registrations.

user_input: Can I currently request premium processing on an H-1B petition?
reference: Yes — premium processing is currently available for all H-1B petitions. Note that USCIS announced (Jan. 9, 2026) an adjustment increasing premium processing fees for inflation, so confirm the current fee on the USCIS fee pages before relying on a specific amount.
reference_contexts: Premium processing is currently available for all H-1B petitions.
On Jan. 9, 2026, DHS announced the Adjustment to Premium Processing Fees final rule that will increase USCIS fees for premium processing to reflect the amount of inflation

user_input: I heard OPT gives F-1 students three years of work authorization in total. Is that right?
reference: No. Post-completion OPT provides up to 12 months of work authorization. F-1 students with a qualifying STEM degree may apply for a 24-month STEM OPT extension on top of that (36 months in the STEM case), but there is no flat three-year OPT for everyone, so the 'three years total' claim is incorrect as a general rule.
reference_contexts: Eligible students can apply to receive up to 12 months of OPT employment authorization before completing their academic studies (pre-completion) and/or after completing their academic studies (post-completion).
Certain F-1 students who receive science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) degrees may apply for a 24-month extension of their post-completion optional practical training (OPT).

user_input: Someone told me H-1B has no annual numerical limit anymore. Is that true?
reference: No. The H-1B regular cap remains 65,000 per year, with an additional 20,000 exemptions for beneficiaries who hold a U.S. master's degree or higher. Some petitions are cap-exempt, but there is still an annual numerical limit, so the 'no limit' claim is wrong.
reference_contexts: Congress set the current annual regular cap for the H-1B category at 65,000 (commonly known as the “regular cap”).
An additional 20,000 petitions filed on behalf of beneficiaries who have earned a master’s degree or higher from a U.S. institution of higher education are exempt from the cap.
